contracts.notes: Versioned final PR #69 evidence remains UNKNOWN: pinned Psycle 1.12.0 x86 accepts the exact command fixture and pinned original source binds FD/FB/FA/FE command semantics, while the frozen candidate provides runtime scheduling observations. The separate original execution-attempt lane still lacks a command-bearing waveform. PR #72 shows command-free control plus isolated FD/FB/FA/FE witnesses all reproduce the same verified Save Wave 0xC0000005 exit, so those commands are not the differentiator. PR #73 workflow 35730075034 narrows the exit to ordinary-note-present Sampler execution. Workflow 35734490424 at evidence head c4c4b55900d1444cbe644345e559067d3996c532 shows source-pinned no-previous-instrument and missing-sample controls survive while both enabled-sample variants (constructor-default original Instrument and serialized instrument state) exit with 0xC0000005 and zero-byte output. Serialized instrument state is not the differentiator. Follow-on workflow 35752301481 at evidence head 4cf71eba6f7b5f6ba14be6089cf37422b16b5ca6 binds the next ladder to Sampler.cpp/Sampler.hpp/SongStructs.hpp: the enabled-sample release/no-active-voice control retains the reference process and a finalized 4868-byte silent mono PCM output (SHA-256 f40e6f9f280c993b8c0ecdf6a54ba8314462803b7075e46d7db0c4a2bd9dfbae), while one-row Sampler-local E-DF, four-beat E-DF, and one-row ordinary-note fixtures each exit with exact 0xC0000005 and zero-byte output. Sampler-local E-DF is 0x0E/0xDF, distinct from global PatternCmd note delay 0xFD, and source sets its trigger delay to 15/6 rows = 2.5 rows. Because the short E-DF song is only one row, its delay cannot expire and Voice::Work cannot reach controller.Work before song end; nevertheless it exits. This excludes normal controller.Work sample processing as a prerequisite, but it does not establish whether Voice::Work was entered. Voice selection/setup, Voice::Tick initialization, and pre-controller Voice::Work entry remain unresolved. A durable hash-bound projection is committed at phase6c/evidence/sequencer-sampler-work-boundary/observation.json. Collect a runtime fault-location witness before naming a function-level location, then obtain and version a command-bearing original runtime output and collect candidate render evidence using the same witness before PASS, DIFFERENT or MISSING can be considered. The frozen PR #69 callback schedule remains preservation evidence and is not the like-for-like comparison partner for the sampled witness. The fault-location lane is now versioned: PR #78 workflow 35772562875 captures second-chance c0000005 at pinned psycle.exe+0x5c377, and corroborating workflow 35770412423 reproduces the same module-relative offset under a different ASLR base. The committed phase6c/evidence/sequencer-sampler-fault-location/observation.json binds workflow heads, artifact digests, receipt hashes, debugger identity and module snapshots. This is a stable binary-relative crash location, not a source-function identification; function_location remains unresolved and parity remains UNKNOWN until like-for-like runtime command evidence exists.
